title: Plate Tectonics and Earthquakes (KS3/4 Geography)
subject: Geography
strapline: Why the Earth’s surface moves, and what happens at plate boundaries.
facts: The Earth’s crust is broken into large tectonic plates that float on the semi-molten mantle below.
Plates move slowly, driven by convection currents in the mantle.
At a destructive (convergent) boundary, plates move together; oceanic crust is subducted, causing volcanoes and powerful earthquakes.
At a constructive (divergent) boundary, plates move apart and new crust forms (e.g. Mid-Atlantic Ridge).
At a conservative (transform) boundary, plates slide past each other, causing earthquakes (e.g. San Andreas Fault).
The focus is where an earthquake starts underground; the epicentre is the point directly above it on the surface.
Earthquake strength is measured on the Richter (or moment magnitude) scale using a seismometer.

quick_quiz.q: What drives the movement of tectonic plates?

quick_quiz.a: the point on the surface directly above the focus
